newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia Congress elects ex-dictator as president.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia Congress elects ex-dictator as president.

text.p: Bolivia's Congress elected former military dictator Hugo Banzer as president on Tuesday after he forged unlikely alliances with leftist and populist parties.
Banzer, who ruled from 1971-78, will be sworn in on Wednesday, Independence Day, to replace President Gonzalo Sanchez de Losada, who was barred by law from running again.

Banzer, 71, won general elections on June 1 as candidate of the right-wing National Democratic Party. But he failed to clinch an absolute majority, forcing Congress to cast a second-round vote between him and runner-up Juan Carlos Duran from the ruling, centrist Nationalist Revolutionary Movement.

In the congressional vote early on Tuesday, Banzer got sufficient support to secure the presidency after only two-thirds of the legislators voted, when he already had the 79 votes needed out of a total of 157.

Banzer had also won the popular vote in 1985 but lost to a rival in the vote in Congress. To avoid a similar fate this time, he allied himself with the Revolutionary Left Movement of ex-President Jaime Paz Zamora and two populist parties, including the Solidarity Civic Union led by millionaire Ivo Kuljis. Paz Zamora and Kuljis came in third and fourth in the presidential polls.
These four parties, allied to smaller groups, won 72 percent of the June 1 vote.
The coalition had already showed its clout last Saturday when its candidates were named heads of the all-new Senate and Lower House.
Banzer will be the first democratically-elected president to rule for five years instead of four under a recent constitutional reform.

He has endorsed a 12-year-old free-market and privatisation drive, but warned the economic model was becoming "dehumanized" and steps were needed to fight poverty. He also promised to revise privatisation contracts to put an end to private monopolies and further open up the economy.
